method: Amounts follow the classic home roux rule: one level tablespoon of all-purpose flour per US cup of liquid for a thin soup, two for a medium sauce and three for a thick gravy or stew. A US cup is 236.5882365 mL and a level US tablespoon is 14.7868 mL, so one, two and three tablespoons per cup work out to about 3.4, 6.8 and 10.1 percent flour by weight in a water-like liquid. Liquid volume is accepted in US cups from 0.25 to 25, millilitres from 60 to 6000 or litres from 0.06 to 6; it is converted to millilitres and one millilitre is taken as one gram, so milk or stock, which are a few percent denser, shift the percentages by a few tenths. A level tablespoon of all-purpose flour is taken as 8 g and a level tablespoon of butter as 14.2 g. The fat is measured to match the flour's volume, the usual kitchen ratio, which comes to 1.78 times the flour's weight. Flour grams are the liquid in cups times the tablespoons per cup times 8, butter grams are the same tablespoon count times 14.2, the roux weight is their sum, and the flour share is flour grams divided by the liquid mass. The reverse mode takes a roux weight from 5 to 2000 g, splits it 8 to 14.2 into flour and butter, turns the flour back into tablespoons and divides by the selected tablespoons per cup to get the liquid it thickens; a roux that would thicken more than 6000 mL is refused because the documented liquid range ends there. Grams and millilitres are reported to one decimal and whole millilitres, cups and tablespoons to two decimals, and percentages to one decimal, all rounded half away from zero. The estimate ignores evaporation, the flour's continued absorption as a sauce stands, gluten-free blends and cornstarch slurries, and it carries no salt; it is a cooking estimate, not food-safety guidance. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Classic roux rule: equal volumes of fat and flour, one level tablespoon of each per cup of liquid for a thin sauce, two for a medium sauce and three for a thick sauce or gravy.
US customary volume conversions used here: 1 US cup = 236.5882365 mL and 1 US tablespoon = 14.7868 mL.
Kitchen densities used to turn tablespoons into grams: all-purpose flour about 8 g and butter about 14.2 g per level US tablespoon.
